comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT. Edits of an imported .f3d design recompute (mitcad#1904, GitHub #371), on the reported design (imported with mitcad-cli import-f3d, never committed; tools/cli/f3d-edit-reported-test.cmake). Its last component holds one body (F14.b0): a base, a tower on it (the extrusion F25 of 43 mm, d37), a support beside the tower (F27, 4 mm, d49), two tie-wrap cuts through it (F32 on the sketch's plane, F33 a 3 mm cut, d63, that starts on a construction plane higher up), chamfers, and a fillet (F35) that comes in as the file's bodies. Before the fix the record of F33 was read 10 bytes off (its start plane's selection was not recognised), so F33 came in as the file's bodies too and replaced the body after the tower: an edit of the tower changed nothing. Now F33 is a parametric cut, and the edits recompute every feature after them.
Before the fillet that came in as the file's bodies (F35, whose rounds the geometry kernel cannot build: mitcad#1819), the tower is 7 mm higher: its top at -497 instead of -504.

Fillet1's rounding of 3 (d96) along the fin's foot and of 0.5 (d98) along its top's edges, each added alone at the state before the fillet (mitcad#1926). The fin's arms are 2 thick, their outer sides lower than 3; the geometry kernel runs the rounding on over those sides' planes and cuts it by the fin's top, which grows out to meet it (OCCT port patch 1700). The roundings of 0.5 along the top's outer and inner edges, two chains apart that the kernel finds overlapping where the arms run down to the plate, are built one after the other. The whole of Fillet1, all its sets at once, still comes in as the file's bodies.
